# certstream-server-rust

> A Certificate Transparency log streaming server written in Rust. It monitors Chrome- and Apple-trusted CT logs and streams newly issued TLS certificates over WebSocket and SSE. It supports both RFC 6962 and static-ct-api logs in one binary and works with existing Certstream clients.

Typical uses include phishing and typosquat detection, brand monitoring, attack surface discovery, threat intelligence pipelines, certificate inventory, and research on newly issued certificates.

On one measured deployment, the server processed around 420 certificates and 700 domain names per second, or roughly 36 million certificates and 62 million domain names per day, while using about 80 MB RSS and 0.2 CPU cores.

## Docs

- [Home](https://certstream.dev/): project overview, installation options, and features
- [API documentation](https://certstream.dev/docs.html): WebSocket and SSE endpoints, message formats, environment variables, and REST API
- [Hosted CertStream API](https://certstream.dev/hosted-api.html): a hosted CertStream-compatible WebSocket API at api.certstream.dev, API key from $2 a month through GitHub Sponsors
- [Quick start](https://certstream.dev/quickstart.html): running the server and connecting a client
- [Architecture](https://certstream.dev/architecture.html): ingest pipeline, broadcast path, deduplication, and state persistence
